summary: Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (~1840-1842) and Harvard University (~1842-1846). He later held a post at King's College London (~1862-1869).

Flavio A. Geisshuesler works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the universities of Bern, Lausanne, and Virginia (PhD under David Germano), and held a postdoctoral post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2019) mentored by Dan Martin.

Florin Deleanu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg (PhD under Lambert Schmithausen), and held professorships at Kansai Medical University (~1997-2001) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2001).
Florinda De Simini is an Indologist who held posts at the University of Naples Federico II (~2015-2018) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2019).

Francesco Sferra is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Raffaele Torella. He held a professorship at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2002) and a post at the University of Naples Federico II (attested 2010).
Francis Buchanan-Hamilton was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served in the Indian Medical Service (~1794-1815) and succeeded Henry Thomas Colebrooke.

Francis Gladwin worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He was a founding member of the Asiatic Society (~1784-1812) and served as a professor of Persian at Fort William College (~1801).

Francis H. Cook worked in Buddhist and religious studies, earning his doctorate from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He served as a professor at UC Riverside (~1970-1990) and became Chair at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 1999.

Francis N. J. is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed a Master's in Ancient History at the University of Calicut and studied under doctoral supervisor M. R. Raghava Varier (attested 2002).
Francis Robinson is a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Bexhill College and became a professor at Royal Holloway, University of London (~1973).
Francis Tiso is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his education at Cornell University, Harvard Divinity School, and Columbia University.
Francis Woodman Cleaves was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, sinology, and linguistics. He studied at Harvard University (~1933-1942) and later served on its faculty (~1946-1980).

Francis X. Clooney is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Fordham University and the University of Chicago. He held professorships and directorships at Boston College (1984), Oxford (~2002-2004, 2005), and Harvard University (2005).
Francisco García Ayuso worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under Martin Haug (~1869-1872).

Francisco Varela was a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Chile and Harvard University. He founded the Mind & Life Institute and held posts at the University of Chile, École Polytechnique, and CNRS (~1986-2001).

Franciscus Verellen is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and history. He studied at Oxford and EPHE (under Kristofer Schipper), and served as a professor (~1991-2021) and director (2004-2014) at the École française d'Extrême-Orient.
Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaii and completed doctoral work under Stewart Sutherland.

Frank Raymond Allchin was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of London. He held academic posts at SOAS (~1951-1954), the University of Cambridge (~1954-1989), and the Ancient India and Iran Trust (~1978-2010).

Frank-Richard Hamm was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate under Walther Schubring at the University of Hamburg, later teaching there (~1958-1964) before becoming Professor of Indology at the University of Bonn (1965).

Franklin Edgerton was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He held professorships at the University of Pennsylvania (1913-1926) and Yale University (from 1926).
